source.name: Harvard Health — Get low with deep squats

entries.evidence: Harvard Health identifies the deep low squat as the posture commonly known as the Asian squat and describes dropping into, holding, and rising from the squat without apparatus.
entries.reason: The identified exercise is a self-supported deep squat; apparatus is not structurally required.

source.name: U.S. Army ATP 7-22.01 — Bend and Reach

entries.evidence: Official Army doctrine defines the complete Bend and Reach starting position and movement using only the body and ground; no apparatus is part of the standardized exercise.
entries.reason: The official standardized movement is equipment-independent.

source.name: ACE — A Beginner's Guide to Sun Salutations

entries.evidence: ACE describes Chair by lowering the hips with body weight in the heels and placing the hands on thighs, in prayer, or reaching forward; a physical chair is not part of the movement.
entries.reason: The canonical wording denotes the yoga chair-position squat, not use of chair apparatus.

source.name: ACE — A Beginner's Guide to Sun Salutations

entries.evidence: ACE describes Forward Fold using body position and optional hand placement on the floor, shins or thighs, with no implement required.
entries.reason: The technical description establishes a floor/body-position movement without required apparatus.

entries.evidence: AHA lists walking and jogging as endurance activities themselves, distinct from equipment-dependent examples such as biking and jumping rope.
entries.reason: Jogging/running is locomotion and does not structurally require exercise apparatus.

source.name: NSCA — Basics of Strength and Conditioning Manual

entries.evidence: NSCA prescribes 50-yard and hollow sprint drills as running intervals over distance; the sprint itself requires no exercise implement.
entries.reason: The canonical locomotion movement is equipment-independent; timing or distance markers are not structural exercise apparatus.

source.name: American Heart Association — Create a Circuit Home Workout

entries.evidence: AHA explicitly presents Star jumps in a home circuit that can be performed without any special equipment.
entries.reason: Exercise-specific inclusion in a no-special-equipment circuit establishes no required apparatus.
